title: Mission lock + sequential execution law
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Confirm the project mission and create the binding no-skip task law.
instructions: Read START_HERE.md, PROJECT_MANIFEST.yaml, AI_CONSTITUTION.md, ADR-0035, ADR-0036.
Create docs/tasks/GOALS.md with the mission, pillars, and execution law.
Record that tasks execute strictly in numeric order (task N+1 only after N done).
acceptance: docs/tasks/GOALS.md exists and states the no-skip rule.

title: Environment + baseline verification
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Prove the toolchain and all existing smoke suites are green before new work.
instructions: Install/verify python deps (pip install -e code/aiosh-mcp) and node deps.
Run all existing smokes: classifier, mcp, pentest, sandbox, demo, cli bash.
Record PASS output in docs/tasks/evidence/T-00002-baseline.md.
acceptance: All baseline suites PASS; evidence captured.

title: Generate canonical 10,000-task ledger
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Create the machine-readable sequential ledger and live task pointer.
instructions: Run tools/generate_master_tasks.py to produce MASTER_TASK_LEDGER.jsonl + TASK_STATE.json.
Verify exactly 10,000 tasks, IDs T-00001..T-10000, each with instructions + acceptance.
Verify next_task pointer equals 4.
acceptance: Ledger has 10,000 well-formed tasks; pointer file exists.

title: Create fail-fast CI runner
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Give the project one command that runs every smoke suite sequentially and fails loudly.
instructions: Create ci/run_all_smokes.sh invoking each suite in order with set -euo pipefail.
Print a per-suite PASS/FAIL summary and exit non-zero on any failure.
Make it executable and run it once; capture output as evidence.
acceptance: bash ci/run_all_smokes.sh exits 0 with all suites PASS.

title: Task-state completion tool
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Provide a single command to mark the active task complete and advance the pointer.
instructions: Create tools/complete_task.py <task_id>: validate task_id == current next_task.
On success, move task to completed set and increment next_task by exactly 1.
Refuse out-of-order completion (this mechanically enforces the no-skip law).
acceptance: complete_task.py rejects wrong-order IDs and advances pointer correctly.

title: Index task system from README
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Make the task ledger discoverable from the repo entry points.
instructions: Add a short section to README.md and docs/README.md pointing at docs/tasks/.
State the rule: agents must read TASK_STATE.json and execute only next_task.
acceptance: README links the ledger and states the no-skip rule.

title: Retention operations runbook
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Document day-2 operations for the Sprint-3 retention system.
instructions: Write docs/RUNBOOK-AUDIT-RETENTION.md covering rotate, verify --full, seen, disaster recovery.
Include copy-paste CLI + MCP examples and what each alarm means.
acceptance: Runbook exists with working examples for all four operations.

title: Backup & sync verification
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Prove the Drive/R2 backup path captures the current tree reproducibly.
instructions: Re-create the AIOS_MERGED.zip snapshot and verify key files byte-match the tree.
Record the procedure + checksums in docs/tasks/evidence/T-00008-backup.md.
acceptance: Backup archive verified; procedure documented.

title: Retention security review
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Threat-model the rotation/archive/seen surfaces shipped in Sprint 3.
instructions: Review rotate/seen/verify_full for injection, path traversal, and covert-erasure abuse.
Confirm MCP rotate requires grant and refusal rows are written.
Record findings in docs/tasks/evidence/T-00009-security.md.
acceptance: Security review evidence file exists; no open bypass.

title: Audit-ring performance baseline
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Measure verify/rotate cost at 10k and 100k rows to size retention cadence.
instructions: Generate synthetic rings (10k, 100k rows) in a temp DB; time verify and verify --full.
Record numbers + recommended rotation cadence in docs/tasks/evidence/T-00010-perf.md.
acceptance: Benchmark table exists with a recommended max live-row threshold.

phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution

phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution

instructions: Define inputs, outputs, error cases, and persistence effects for data model.

instructions: Write a failing test first where feasible (smoke or unit).

Do not add new dependencies unless the Research task for this epic approved one.
Keep all audit/PEP invariants: consequential actions write exactly one audit row.

No regression in existing smoke suites for touched modules.

phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution

title: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution / Task Ledger Control / data model: Security Review
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Security-review the data model of Task Ledger Control.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-00017-security.md.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution / Task Ledger Control / data model: Hardening
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Harden the data model of Task Ledger Control against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

goal: Add focused automated tests for the MCP/API surface of Agent Handoff Protocol.
instructions: Cover: valid input, invalid input, boundary values, and the primary failure mode.
Add tests under the matching tests/ directory using the existing smoke-test style.
Assert observable behavior (return values, DB state, files), not implementation details.
Run the new test file in isolation and confirm it fails when the feature is broken.
acceptance: New test file runs standalone and passes.
Negative cases are asserted, not just happy path.

title: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution / Agent Handoff Protocol / MCP/API surface: Integration
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Integrate the MCP/API surface of Agent Handoff Protocol with the surrounding system.
instructions: Wire the feature into its real call path (CLI command, MCP tool, or service hook).
Confirm cross-substrate parity where the feature touches the shared SQLite DB or canonical JSON.
Update the relevant server/CLI registration point so the surface is discoverable.
Run the closest existing smoke suite that exercises the integrated path.
acceptance: Feature reachable through its production surface.
Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution / Agent Handoff Protocol / MCP/API surface: Security Review
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Security-review the MCP/API surface of Agent Handoff Protocol.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-00947-security.md.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution / Agent Handoff Protocol / MCP/API surface: Hardening
phase: Phase 0 — Governance, Repo, CI, Task Execution
goal: Harden the MCP/API surface of Agent Handoff Protocol against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

goal: Harden the configuration of Base Image Build against failure and misuse.

No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

goal: Harden the MCP/API surface of Session Isolation against failure and misuse.

No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 3 — AI Control Plane (Pillar C Spine) / Evaluation Harness / core service: Security Review
phase: Phase 3 — AI Control Plane (Pillar C Spine)
goal: Security-review the core service of Evaluation Harness.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-03979-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 3 — AI Control Plane (Pillar C Spine) / Evaluation Harness / core service: Hardening
phase: Phase 3 — AI Control Plane (Pillar C Spine)
goal: Harden the core service of Evaluation Harness against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

instructions: Create or extend the appropriate source file(s) under code/ following existing module style.

Wire exports/imports so the project still compiles or imports cleanly.
Run the build (npm run build / python -c import) and fix all errors.
acceptance: Project builds/imports with zero errors.
New interfaces exist and are referenced by at least one call site or test stub.

title: Phase 5 — Pillar B: Windows-Style Desktop / Windows-Look Theme Engine / core service: Implementation
goal: Implement the minimal working behavior for the core service of Windows-Look Theme Engine.
instructions: Write a failing test first where feasible (smoke or unit).
Implement the smallest change that passes; follow existing patterns in code/aiosh-cli and code/aiosh-mcp.
Reuse existing helpers (audit ring, dispatch gate, classifier) instead of duplicating logic.
Do not add new dependencies unless the Research task for this epic approved one.
Keep all audit/PEP invariants: consequential actions write exactly one audit row.

No regression in existing smoke suites for touched modules.

title: Phase 5 — Pillar B: Windows-Style Desktop / Windows-Look Theme Engine / core service: Unit Test
goal: Add focused automated tests for the core service of Windows-Look Theme Engine.

Run the new test file in isolation and confirm it fails when the feature is broken.

Negative cases are asserted, not just happy path.

title: Phase 5 — Pillar B: Windows-Style Desktop / Windows-Look Theme Engine / core service: Integration
goal: Integrate the core service of Windows-Look Theme Engine with the surrounding system.
instructions: Wire the feature into its real call path (CLI command, MCP tool, or service hook).
Confirm cross-substrate parity where the feature touches the shared SQLite DB or canonical JSON.
Update the relevant server/CLI registration point so the surface is discoverable.
Run the closest existing smoke suite that exercises the integrated path.
acceptance: Feature reachable through its production surface.
Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 5 — Pillar B: Windows-Style Desktop / Windows-Look Theme Engine / core service: Security Review
goal: Security-review the core service of Windows-Look Theme Engine.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-05679-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 5 — Pillar B: Windows-Style Desktop / Windows-Look Theme Engine / core service: Hardening
goal: Harden the core service of Windows-Look Theme Engine against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

goal: Harden the data model of GUI Session Security against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.

No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

instructions: Create or extend the appropriate source file(s) under code/ following existing module style.
Define typed function signatures / interfaces only; bodies fail loudly (throw/NotImplementedError).
Wire exports/imports so the project still compiles or imports cleanly.
Run the build (npm run build / python -c import) and fix all errors.
acceptance: Project builds/imports with zero errors.
New interfaces exist and are referenced by at least one call site or test stub.

title: Phase 7 — Storage, Networking, Devices / Display & Input Stack / MCP/API surface: Implementation
goal: Implement the minimal working behavior for the MCP/API surface of Display & Input Stack.
instructions: Write a failing test first where feasible (smoke or unit).
Implement the smallest change that passes; follow existing patterns in code/aiosh-cli and code/aiosh-mcp.
Reuse existing helpers (audit ring, dispatch gate, classifier) instead of duplicating logic.
Do not add new dependencies unless the Research task for this epic approved one.
Keep all audit/PEP invariants: consequential actions write exactly one audit row.
acceptance: Targeted test passes.
No regression in existing smoke suites for touched modules.

title: Phase 7 — Storage, Networking, Devices / Display & Input Stack / MCP/API surface: Unit Test
goal: Add focused automated tests for the MCP/API surface of Display & Input Stack.
instructions: Cover: valid input, invalid input, boundary values, and the primary failure mode.
Add tests under the matching tests/ directory using the existing smoke-test style.
Assert observable behavior (return values, DB state, files), not implementation details.
Run the new test file in isolation and confirm it fails when the feature is broken.
acceptance: New test file runs standalone and passes.
Negative cases are asserted, not just happy path.

title: Phase 7 — Storage, Networking, Devices / Display & Input Stack / MCP/API surface: Integration
goal: Integrate the MCP/API surface of Display & Input Stack with the surrounding system.
instructions: Wire the feature into its real call path (CLI command, MCP tool, or service hook).
Confirm cross-substrate parity where the feature touches the shared SQLite DB or canonical JSON.
Update the relevant server/CLI registration point so the surface is discoverable.
Run the closest existing smoke suite that exercises the integrated path.
acceptance: Feature reachable through its production surface.
Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 7 — Storage, Networking, Devices / Display & Input Stack / MCP/API surface: Security Review
goal: Security-review the MCP/API surface of Display & Input Stack.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-07699-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 7 — Storage, Networking, Devices / Display & Input Stack / MCP/API surface: Hardening
goal: Harden the MCP/API surface of Display & Input Stack against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

title: Phase 7 — Storage, Networking, Devices / Display & Input Stack / MCP/API surface: Documentation
goal: Document the MCP/API surface of Display & Input Stack for operators and agents.
instructions: Update the relevant README/spec with what shipped and how to invoke it.
Include at least one copy-pasteable example command or tool call.
Record constraints and known limitations honestly.
Link the task evidence files from the doc.
acceptance: Docs updated with working example.
Limitations are stated, not omitted.

title: Phase 7 — Storage, Networking, Devices / Display & Input Stack / MCP/API surface: Verification & Evidence
goal: Verify the MCP/API surface of Display & Input Stack and close the task with evidence.
instructions: Run all test suites relevant to this epic plus the full baseline smoke set.
Capture PASS output into docs/tasks/evidence/T-07702-verify.md.

State files updated; next task pointer advanced.

instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-08109-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Metrics Collection / configuration: Hardening
goal: Harden the configuration of Metrics Collection against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

instructions: Update the relevant README/spec with what shipped and how to invoke it.

instructions: Write a failing test first where feasible (smoke or unit).
Implement the smallest change that passes; follow existing patterns in code/aiosh-cli and code/aiosh-mcp.
Reuse existing helpers (audit ring, dispatch gate, classifier) instead of duplicating logic.
Do not add new dependencies unless the Research task for this epic approved one.
Keep all audit/PEP invariants: consequential actions write exactly one audit row.
acceptance: Targeted test passes.
No regression in existing smoke suites for touched modules.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Crash Recovery / automated tests: Unit Test
goal: Add focused automated tests for the automated tests of Crash Recovery.
instructions: Cover: valid input, invalid input, boundary values, and the primary failure mode.
Add tests under the matching tests/ directory using the existing smoke-test style.
Assert observable behavior (return values, DB state, files), not implementation details.
Run the new test file in isolation and confirm it fails when the feature is broken.
acceptance: New test file runs standalone and passes.
Negative cases are asserted, not just happy path.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Crash Recovery / automated tests: Integration
goal: Integrate the automated tests of Crash Recovery with the surrounding system.
instructions: Wire the feature into its real call path (CLI command, MCP tool, or service hook).
Confirm cross-substrate parity where the feature touches the shared SQLite DB or canonical JSON.
Update the relevant server/CLI registration point so the surface is discoverable.
Run the closest existing smoke suite that exercises the integrated path.
acceptance: Feature reachable through its production surface.
Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Crash Recovery / automated tests: Security Review
goal: Security-review the automated tests of Crash Recovery.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-08419-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Crash Recovery / automated tests: Hardening
goal: Harden the automated tests of Crash Recovery against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Crash Recovery / automated tests: Documentation
goal: Document the automated tests of Crash Recovery for operators and agents.
instructions: Update the relevant README/spec with what shipped and how to invoke it.
Include at least one copy-pasteable example command or tool call.
Record constraints and known limitations honestly.
Link the task evidence files from the doc.
acceptance: Docs updated with working example.
Limitations are stated, not omitted.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Crash Recovery / automated tests: Verification & Evidence

instructions: Cover: valid input, invalid input, boundary values, and the primary failure mode.
Add tests under the matching tests/ directory using the existing smoke-test style.
Assert observable behavior (return values, DB state, files), not implementation details.
Run the new test file in isolation and confirm it fails when the feature is broken.
acceptance: New test file runs standalone and passes.
Negative cases are asserted, not just happy path.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Health Checks / data model: Integration
goal: Integrate the data model of Health Checks with the surrounding system.
instructions: Wire the feature into its real call path (CLI command, MCP tool, or service hook).
Confirm cross-substrate parity where the feature touches the shared SQLite DB or canonical JSON.
Update the relevant server/CLI registration point so the surface is discoverable.
Run the closest existing smoke suite that exercises the integrated path.
acceptance: Feature reachable through its production surface.
Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Health Checks / data model: Security Review
goal: Security-review the data model of Health Checks.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-08469-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Health Checks / data model: Hardening
goal: Harden the data model of Health Checks against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

instructions: Wire the feature into its real call path (CLI command, MCP tool, or service hook).
Confirm cross-substrate parity where the feature touches the shared SQLite DB or canonical JSON.
Update the relevant server/CLI registration point so the surface is discoverable.
Run the closest existing smoke suite that exercises the integrated path.
acceptance: Feature reachable through its production surface.
Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Health Checks / automated tests: Security Review
goal: Security-review the automated tests of Health Checks.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-08519-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Health Checks / automated tests: Hardening
goal: Harden the automated tests of Health Checks against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

goal: Document the automated tests of Health Checks for operators and agents.
instructions: Update the relevant README/spec with what shipped and how to invoke it.

List unknowns and decisions needed before any implementation task.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Resource Limits / core service: Specification
goal: Specify the exact contract for the core service of Resource Limits.
instructions: Define inputs, outputs, error cases, and persistence effects for core service.
State which existing interfaces are reused and which are new.
Write the spec section to docs/tasks/evidence/T-08674-spec.md.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Resource Limits / core service: Scaffold
goal: Create the module skeleton and interfaces for the core service of Resource Limits.
instructions: Create or extend the appropriate source file(s) under code/ following existing module style.
Define typed function signatures / interfaces only; bodies fail loudly (throw/NotImplementedError).
Wire exports/imports so the project still compiles or imports cleanly.
Run the build (npm run build / python -c import) and fix all errors.
acceptance: Project builds/imports with zero errors.
New interfaces exist and are referenced by at least one call site or test stub.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Resource Limits / core service: Implementation
goal: Implement the minimal working behavior for the core service of Resource Limits.
instructions: Write a failing test first where feasible (smoke or unit).
Implement the smallest change that passes; follow existing patterns in code/aiosh-cli and code/aiosh-mcp.
Reuse existing helpers (audit ring, dispatch gate, classifier) instead of duplicating logic.
Do not add new dependencies unless the Research task for this epic approved one.
Keep all audit/PEP invariants: consequential actions write exactly one audit row.
acceptance: Targeted test passes.
No regression in existing smoke suites for touched modules.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Resource Limits / core service: Unit Test
goal: Add focused automated tests for the core service of Resource Limits.
instructions: Cover: valid input, invalid input, boundary values, and the primary failure mode.
Add tests under the matching tests/ directory using the existing smoke-test style.
Assert observable behavior (return values, DB state, files), not implementation details.
Run the new test file in isolation and confirm it fails when the feature is broken.
acceptance: New test file runs standalone and passes.
Negative cases are asserted, not just happy path.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Resource Limits / core service: Integration
goal: Integrate the core service of Resource Limits with the surrounding system.
instructions: Wire the feature into its real call path (CLI command, MCP tool, or service hook).
Confirm cross-substrate parity where the feature touches the shared SQLite DB or canonical JSON.
Update the relevant server/CLI registration point so the surface is discoverable.
Run the closest existing smoke suite that exercises the integrated path.
acceptance: Feature reachable through its production surface.
Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Resource Limits / core service: Security Review
goal: Security-review the core service of Resource Limits.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-08679-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Resource Limits / core service: Hardening
goal: Harden the core service of Resource Limits against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

instructions: Read the existing code and docs related to core service before assuming anything is missing.
Collect authoritative sources (upstream docs, man pages, RFCs) and record fact vs assumption.
Write findings to docs/tasks/evidence/T-08773-research.md with citations.
List unknowns and decisions needed before any implementation task.
acceptance: Evidence file exists and separates facts from assumptions.
No code changed; decisions needed are listed explicitly.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Chaos Testing / core service: Specification
goal: Specify the exact contract for the core service of Chaos Testing.
instructions: Define inputs, outputs, error cases, and persistence effects for core service.
State which existing interfaces are reused and which are new.
Write the spec section to docs/tasks/evidence/T-08774-spec.md.
Do not invent APIs that do not exist upstream; mark any proposal as AIOS-specific.
acceptance: Spec covers happy path, failure path, and audit effects.
Spec is reviewable without reading the implementation.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Chaos Testing / core service: Scaffold
goal: Create the module skeleton and interfaces for the core service of Chaos Testing.
instructions: Create or extend the appropriate source file(s) under code/ following existing module style.
Define typed function signatures / interfaces only; bodies fail loudly (throw/NotImplementedError).
Wire exports/imports so the project still compiles or imports cleanly.
Run the build (npm run build / python -c import) and fix all errors.
acceptance: Project builds/imports with zero errors.
New interfaces exist and are referenced by at least one call site or test stub.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Chaos Testing / core service: Implementation
goal: Implement the minimal working behavior for the core service of Chaos Testing.
instructions: Write a failing test first where feasible (smoke or unit).
Implement the smallest change that passes; follow existing patterns in code/aiosh-cli and code/aiosh-mcp.
Reuse existing helpers (audit ring, dispatch gate, classifier) instead of duplicating logic.
Do not add new dependencies unless the Research task for this epic approved one.
Keep all audit/PEP invariants: consequential actions write exactly one audit row.
acceptance: Targeted test passes.
No regression in existing smoke suites for touched modules.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Chaos Testing / core service: Unit Test
goal: Add focused automated tests for the core service of Chaos Testing.
instructions: Cover: valid input, invalid input, boundary values, and the primary failure mode.
Add tests under the matching tests/ directory using the existing smoke-test style.
Assert observable behavior (return values, DB state, files), not implementation details.
Run the new test file in isolation and confirm it fails when the feature is broken.
acceptance: New test file runs standalone and passes.
Negative cases are asserted, not just happy path.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Chaos Testing / core service: Integration
goal: Integrate the core service of Chaos Testing with the surrounding system.
instructions: Wire the feature into its real call path (CLI command, MCP tool, or service hook).
Confirm cross-substrate parity where the feature touches the shared SQLite DB or canonical JSON.
Update the relevant server/CLI registration point so the surface is discoverable.
Run the closest existing smoke suite that exercises the integrated path.
acceptance: Feature reachable through its production surface.
Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Chaos Testing / core service: Security Review
goal: Security-review the core service of Chaos Testing.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-08779-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Chaos Testing / core service: Hardening
goal: Harden the core service of Chaos Testing against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Chaos Testing / core service: Documentation
goal: Document the core service of Chaos Testing for operators and agents.
instructions: Update the relevant README/spec with what shipped and how to invoke it.
Include at least one copy-pasteable example command or tool call.
Record constraints and known limitations honestly.
Link the task evidence files from the doc.
acceptance: Docs updated with working example.
Limitations are stated, not omitted.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Chaos Testing / core service: Verification & Evidence
goal: Verify the core service of Chaos Testing and close the task with evidence.
instructions: Run all test suites relevant to this epic plus the full baseline smoke set.
Capture PASS output into docs/tasks/evidence/T-08782-verify.md.
Update task_plan.md / progress.md if this task completes a milestone.
[PoR] Run the Proof-of-Restraint conformance smoke and anchor verification; if this component touched grants, audit, PEP or dispatch, append an entry to docs/proof-of-restraint/LOG.md.
Only then mark the task complete and advance to the next numeric task.
acceptance: Full relevant suite green with captured output.
State files updated; next task pointer advanced.

instructions: Cover: valid input, invalid input, boundary values, and the primary failure mode.
Add tests under the matching tests/ directory using the existing smoke-test style.
Assert observable behavior (return values, DB state, files), not implementation details.
Run the new test file in isolation and confirm it fails when the feature is broken.
acceptance: New test file runs standalone and passes.
Negative cases are asserted, not just happy path.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Upgrade Safety / security policy: Integration
goal: Integrate the security policy of Upgrade Safety with the surrounding system.
instructions: Wire the feature into its real call path (CLI command, MCP tool, or service hook).
Confirm cross-substrate parity where the feature touches the shared SQLite DB or canonical JSON.
Update the relevant server/CLI registration point so the surface is discoverable.
Run the closest existing smoke suite that exercises the integrated path.
acceptance: Feature reachable through its production surface.
Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Upgrade Safety / security policy: Security Review
goal: Security-review the security policy of Upgrade Safety.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-08929-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Upgrade Safety / security policy: Hardening
goal: Harden the security policy of Upgrade Safety against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

title: Phase 8 — Reliability, Observability, Performance / Upgrade Safety / security policy: Documentation
goal: Document the security policy of Upgrade Safety for operators and agents.
instructions: Update the relevant README/spec with what shipped and how to invoke it.
Include at least one copy-pasteable example command or tool call.
Record constraints and known limitations honestly.
Link the task evidence files from the doc.
acceptance: Docs updated with working example.
Limitations are stated, not omitted.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / Release Engineering / observability: Implementation
goal: Implement the minimal working behavior for the observability of Release Engineering.
instructions: Write a failing test first where feasible (smoke or unit).

goal: Add focused automated tests for the observability of Release Engineering.

Negative cases are asserted, not just happy path.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / Release Engineering / observability: Integration
goal: Integrate the observability of Release Engineering with the surrounding system.
instructions: Wire the feature into its real call path (CLI command, MCP tool, or service hook).

Update the relevant server/CLI registration point so the surface is discoverable.
Run the closest existing smoke suite that exercises the integrated path.
acceptance: Feature reachable through its production surface.
Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / Release Engineering / observability: Security Review
goal: Security-review the observability of Release Engineering.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-09139-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / Release Engineering / observability: Hardening
goal: Harden the observability of Release Engineering against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

instructions: Write a failing test first where feasible (smoke or unit).
Implement the smallest change that passes; follow existing patterns in code/aiosh-cli and code/aiosh-mcp.

Do not add new dependencies unless the Research task for this epic approved one.

No regression in existing smoke suites for touched modules.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / User Onboarding / CLI surface: Unit Test
goal: Add focused automated tests for the CLI surface of User Onboarding.

Add tests under the matching tests/ directory using the existing smoke-test style.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / User Onboarding / CLI surface: Integration
goal: Integrate the CLI surface of User Onboarding with the surrounding system.
instructions: Wire the feature into its real call path (CLI command, MCP tool, or service hook).
Confirm cross-substrate parity where the feature touches the shared SQLite DB or canonical JSON.
Update the relevant server/CLI registration point so the surface is discoverable.
Run the closest existing smoke suite that exercises the integrated path.
acceptance: Feature reachable through its production surface.
Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / User Onboarding / CLI surface: Security Review
goal: Security-review the CLI surface of User Onboarding.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-09389-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / User Onboarding / CLI surface: Hardening
goal: Harden the CLI surface of User Onboarding against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

instructions: Read the existing code and docs related to documentation before assuming anything is missing.
Collect authoritative sources (upstream docs, man pages, RFCs) and record fact vs assumption.
Write findings to docs/tasks/evidence/T-09843-research.md with citations.
List unknowns and decisions needed before any implementation task.
acceptance: Evidence file exists and separates facts from assumptions.
No code changed; decisions needed are listed explicitly.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / Accessibility Review / documentation: Specification
goal: Specify the exact contract for the documentation of Accessibility Review.
instructions: Define inputs, outputs, error cases, and persistence effects for documentation.
State which existing interfaces are reused and which are new.
Write the spec section to docs/tasks/evidence/T-09844-spec.md.
Do not invent APIs that do not exist upstream; mark any proposal as AIOS-specific.
acceptance: Spec covers happy path, failure path, and audit effects.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / Accessibility Review / documentation: Scaffold
goal: Create the module skeleton and interfaces for the documentation of Accessibility Review.
instructions: Create or extend the appropriate source file(s) under code/ following existing module style.
Define typed function signatures / interfaces only; bodies fail loudly (throw/NotImplementedError).
Wire exports/imports so the project still compiles or imports cleanly.
Run the build (npm run build / python -c import) and fix all errors.
acceptance: Project builds/imports with zero errors.
New interfaces exist and are referenced by at least one call site or test stub.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / Accessibility Review / documentation: Implementation
goal: Implement the minimal working behavior for the documentation of Accessibility Review.
instructions: Write a failing test first where feasible (smoke or unit).
Implement the smallest change that passes; follow existing patterns in code/aiosh-cli and code/aiosh-mcp.
Reuse existing helpers (audit ring, dispatch gate, classifier) instead of duplicating logic.
Do not add new dependencies unless the Research task for this epic approved one.
Keep all audit/PEP invariants: consequential actions write exactly one audit row.
acceptance: Targeted test passes.
No regression in existing smoke suites for touched modules.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / Accessibility Review / documentation: Unit Test
goal: Add focused automated tests for the documentation of Accessibility Review.
instructions: Cover: valid input, invalid input, boundary values, and the primary failure mode.
Add tests under the matching tests/ directory using the existing smoke-test style.
Assert observable behavior (return values, DB state, files), not implementation details.
Run the new test file in isolation and confirm it fails when the feature is broken.
acceptance: New test file runs standalone and passes.
Negative cases are asserted, not just happy path.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / Accessibility Review / documentation: Integration
goal: Integrate the documentation of Accessibility Review with the surrounding system.
instructions: Wire the feature into its real call path (CLI command, MCP tool, or service hook).
Confirm cross-substrate parity where the feature touches the shared SQLite DB or canonical JSON.
Update the relevant server/CLI registration point so the surface is discoverable.
Run the closest existing smoke suite that exercises the integrated path.
acceptance: Feature reachable through its production surface.
Integration smoke passes end-to-end.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / Accessibility Review / documentation: Security Review
goal: Security-review the documentation of Accessibility Review.
instructions: Check input validation, path/argument injection, and untrusted-content handling.
Verify PEP gating and audit-row emission for every state-changing path.
Document abuse scenarios in docs/tasks/evidence/T-09849-security.md.

[PoR] Proof-of-Restraint standing rule: if this component adds or changes any state-changing path, confirm it cannot execute without redeeming a capability token (docs/proof-of-restraint/PLAN.md invariant I-2) and record the check in the security evidence.
If any scenario bypasses policy, create a blocking note and fix before proceeding.
acceptance: Security evidence file exists with abuse scenarios.
No known policy bypass remains open.

title: Phase 9 — Release, Certification, User Docs / Accessibility Review / documentation: Hardening
goal: Harden the documentation of Accessibility Review against failure and misuse.
instructions: Add timeouts, size caps, and bounded retries where external processes or files are involved.
Ensure errors are reported in the standard result envelope (never silent failure).
Confirm resource cleanup (DB connections, temp files, child processes).
Fail-open behavior must always write an honest audit row (per ADR-0035 §F-2).
acceptance: Failure modes produce explicit, auditable errors.
No temp/connection leaks on the error path.

goal: Document the documentation of Accessibility Review for operators and agents.

Record constraints and known limitations honestly.
Link the task evidence files from the doc.
acceptance: Docs updated with working example.
Limitations are stated, not omitted.
